experiment.title: Error-amplifier offset budget by Monte Carlo: every term measured, and their sum checked
experiment.claim: Issue #9 -- the DISTRIBUTION half of the error amplifier's offset/mismatch budget, graded against README.md 'Target specification (ratified -- see DR-005, issue #1)'. Measures, on one seed stream at the nominal process point: the amplifier's random input-referred offset in its own loop, the 8x PNP array pair's sigma(dVBE) and absolute VEB, the res_high_po R2/R1 ratio spread, and the resulting total spread of the untrimmed reference -- then checks that the first four reproduce the fifth. This is what design/error-amp-offset-budget.md's allocation is built on. It is NOT the +/-2% untrimmed output-accuracy spec claim (DR-005's ratified figure, formerly a +/-1% draft): this is mismatch only, at one process point, with no global process shift or temperature curvature. That claim is issue #11's experiment / sim/monte-carlo-untrimmed's yield claim. The deterministic half (stability, offset gain, PSRR, Iq) is sim/error-amp-loop/.
experiment.statistical_convention: N = 300 Monte Carlo samples per point, local mismatch only (section tt_mm: MC_MM_SWITCH=1, MC_PR_SWITCH=0); 1 sigma sample standard deviation (N-1), fixed setseed 20260803

mismatch_model.switch: MC_MM_SWITCH (set by the .lib section: 0 in tt/ss/ff/sf/fs, 1 in *_mm)

points.purpose: local-mismatch distribution at the nominal process point

checks.name: sample_count
checks.detail: parsed 300 samples, expected 300

checks.name: mc_solve_yield
checks.detail: 300/300 draws converged to the operating solution (VOUT in 0.9..1.5 V); 0 landed on the core's other stable branch and are excluded from every statistic below. This is a STARTUP observation (issue #10 -- the core has no startup circuit), not a mismatch one, and it is also sensitive to the testbench .nodeset; the threshold here only asserts that enough draws remain for the distribution to mean anything (>= 50%).
